datePolicy: Guide dates describe the latest dated source included, not the date this presentation was built. Date-only values must remain calendar dates. Timeline entries link original publication records and preserve their timestamps.

guides.title: Miami cargo-plane crash: the story so far
guides.intro: A cargo flight overran a runway at Miami International Airport on September 6. The sheriff reported five deaths. Investigators have released preliminary recorder findings; the cited update does not determine a final cause.

known.text: The FAA says 21 Air Flight 7598, a Boeing 767-300 cargo aircraft arriving from San Juan, overran a Miami International Airport runway around 2 p.m. local time on September 6.
known.label: FAA · September 6 incident statement

known.text: WPLG Local 10 reported from the September 6 news conference that the Miami-Dade sheriff said five people had died and five others were hospitalized.
known.label: WPLG Local 10 · Sheriff’s news conference

known.text: The NTSB identifies the runway as Runway 30 and lists investigation DCA26MA352 as ongoing. Its September 9 recorder-data update is preliminary and may change.
known.label: NTSB · Investigation DCA26MA352

unknown.text: The cited NTSB update does not establish a final probable cause. Preliminary recorder observations should not be treated as a finding of responsibility.
These early updates do not establish the injured people’s later conditions. The casualty report above is attributed to the September 6 news conference.

timeline.label: First video update: runway overrun and rescue response
Follow-up: the sheriff’s reported death and injury toll

guides.sourcingNote: This guide connects existing Noteworthy updates with the cited agency documents and credited reporting. The original X posts are distribution records, not independent evidence. The timeline shows when Noteworthy published its updates, not the time each event occurred.

change.title: NTSB adds preliminary recorder evidence
change.text: The September 9 NTSB update adds a preliminary sequence from the cockpit voice and flight data recorders. It is an investigative update, not a final determination of cause.
change.label: NTSB · Investigative update, September 9

guides.title: UW-Whitewater: from campus alert to all-clear
guides.intro: The September 2 warning was followed by an all-clear. Statements from UW-Whitewater and the city say police investigated the report and found no threat. The initial alert should be read alongside that resolution.

known.text: UW-Whitewater says its emergency system was activated while police responded to a report that a person believed to have a weapon had entered Andersen Hall.
known.label: UW-Whitewater · Chancellor and police chief’s statement

known.text: The university says officers later located a person matching the description, found no weapon and determined that there was no threat.
known.label: UW-Whitewater · Account of the police response

known.text: The City of Whitewater’s September 2 statement also reports that police found no threat and the university issued the all-clear.
known.label: City of Whitewater · Police chief and city manager’s statement

unknown.text: The official statements cited here do not specify the exact interval between the initial alert and the all-clear. The timeline below uses our posts’ publication times, not official alert timestamps.

timeline.label: Resolution update: the university says there is no threat

sources.label: UW-Whitewater — Message regarding activation of the emergency alert system
City of Whitewater — Statement regarding the emergency response at UW-Whitewater

guides.sourcingNote: The outcome is attributed to the university and city statements. This guide does not establish that an armed attack occurred: those statements describe a reported threat that police ruled out. The two Noteworthy posts preserve the sequence of the publication’s coverage.

change.title: The reported threat was ruled out
change.text: After the initial campus alert, UW-Whitewater said police located the person, found no weapon and determined there was no threat. That all-clear supersedes the earlier warning.
change.label: UW-Whitewater · September 2 statement

guides.title: Clover Hill cheese recall: what the final FDA update says
guides.intro: The June recall and final August update concern the same outbreak. FDA marks it ended while advising consumers about recalled cheese still in storage.

known.text: Clover Hill Dairy expanded its recall on June 18 to include all of its cheese products because of possible Listeria contamination, according to the company announcement posted by FDA.
known.label: FDA-hosted company announcement · June 18

known.text: The FDA’s August 26 update marks the investigation complete and reports 15 illnesses across four states, 14 hospitalizations and one death.
known.label: FDA · Final outbreak update, August 26

known.text: FDA advises consumers not to eat or serve recalled cheese, and to discard frozen cheese if missing packaging makes it impossible to tell whether it was recalled.
known.label: FDA · Recommendations and product identifiers

unknown.text: FDA notes that recalled products may have reached locations beyond the listed distribution states. States reporting illnesses and places receiving products are different measures.
This brief cannot determine whether a particular package is affected. Compare its identifying information with the FDA’s recalled-product details.

timeline.label: Agency coverage record: published June 29; source updated August 26

sources.label: FDA — Clover Hill Dairy expanded recall announcement
FDA — Soft cheese outbreak investigation and final update

guides.sourcingNote: This guide concerns an ended outbreak. Outcome counts come from the final FDA advisory; earlier automated descriptions may be outdated. No counts from different updates have been added together.

change.title: FDA closes the outbreak investigation
change.text: The August 26 advisory marks the investigation complete and supplies the final reported outcomes. The earlier ongoing-investigation description is historical; the totals are not cumulative additions across updates.
change.label: FDA · Final outbreak update, August 26
